mainTopic: Acquiring from הקדש when prices change; women's obligations in מצוות; a father's duties to his son (מילה and פדיון הבן)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about buying or redeeming an item from הקדש when its price changes. With הקדש, money is what acquires, and a regular person's power should not be stronger than הקדש's. In three of the four cases the buyer pays the higher price, but if he paid 100 and the price then rose, he pays only 100. The גמרא explains that a regular seller could not freely back out either, because of the curse of מי שפרע. A new משנה then teaches which מצוות women are obligated in: father-son duties, time-bound and non-time-bound positive מצוות, and prohibitions, with three exceptions. רב יהודה explains that 'מצוות הבן על האב' means a father's duties toward his son, such as מילה, פדיון הבן, teaching Torah, marrying him off, and teaching a trade. The גמרא finds sources for מילה and פדיון הבן and shows why the mother is not obligated in them. A ברייתא then argues over whether a man redeems himself or his son first. רבי ירמיה begins to limit that argument, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the rule: between regular people, only pulling or taking possession acquires
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its earlier rule: between ordinary people, money alone does not finalize a purchase. The buyer must pull the item or take possession of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: …until he pulls it or takes possession of it.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a sentence from the previous section. Between two ordinary people, a sale is not final until the buyer does משיכה or חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is comparing הקדש with a regular seller. With הקדש, money acquires. With a regular person, only pulling or taking possession acquires. This contrast is the background for all four cases that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling an item toward oneself, a way of acquiring movable things
Taking possession, an act of acquiring
An ordinary person, as opposed to הקדש

phrases.english: until he pulls or takes possession.
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence just before: an ordinary person doesn't acquire with money alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: עד שימשוך ויחזיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's contrast between הקדש (money acquires) and הדיוט (pulling acquires), which began in the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Between ordinary people, a sale becomes final only through משיכה or החזקה, not through money.

steps.title: Case 1: Pulled at 100, price rose to 200 before paying
steps.stepSummary: Someone pulled a הקדש item when it was worth a מנה, but did not pay until it was worth 200. He pays 200, because with הקדש it is the money that acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he pulled it at a מנה (100) and did not manage to redeem it until it went up to 200, he gives 200. What is the reason? The פסוק says: 'He shall give the money and it will be his.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its first case. Pulling does not acquire from הקדש, so the deal only closes when he pays, and by then the price is 200.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק ties acquisition from הקדש to giving money, pulling at 100 did not lock in the price. The item still belongs to הקדש until payment, so he pays the current price of 200.

keyTerms.meaning: To redeem it, meaning to pay הקדש for it
'He shall give the money and it will be his', the source that money acquires from הקדש

phrases.english: If he pulled it at a hundred
phrases.notes: A מנה is 100 זוז. The item is worth that much when he pulls it.

phrases.english: and he did not manage to redeem it
until it stood at two hundred –
he gives two hundred.
What is the reason?
"He shall give the money and it will be his."

steps.triggerLanguage: משכו במנה ולא הספיק לפדותו עד שעמד במאתים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule that money, not pulling, acquires from הקדש to a case where the price went up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pulling alone does not acquire from הקדש. If the price rose before payment, he pays the higher price.

steps.title: Case 2: Pulled at 200, price dropped to 100 before paying
steps.stepSummary: Someone pulled a הקדש item at 200, and the price dropped to 100 before he paid. He still pays 200, because a regular person's power should not be greater than הקדש's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he pulled it at 200 and did not manage to redeem it until it dropped to a מנה, he gives 200. What is the reason? The power of an ordinary person should not be stronger than הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite case, where the price went down. Here pulling does count against the buyer, so he pays 200.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he had pulled this item from a regular seller at 200, the sale would be final at 200. It would be unfair if a regular seller were better protected than הקדש. So הקדש gets the benefit of the pulling too, and he cannot back out to pay the lower price.

keyTerms.term: לֹא יְהֵא כֹּחַ הֶדְיוֹט חָמוּר מֵהֶקְדֵּשׁ
keyTerms.meaning: A regular person's power should not be stronger than הקדש's
Property belonging to the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: It seems strange that pulling doesn't count in Case 1 but does count here. The key is that each rule works in favor of הקדש: money acquires because of the פסוק, and pulling also binds the buyer so הקדש is never weaker than a regular seller.

phrases.english: If he pulled it at two hundred,
and he did not manage to redeem it
until it stood at a hundred –
he gives two hundred.
What is the reason?
The power of an ordinary person should not be
stronger than הקדש.
phrases.notes: Literally 'more severe.' The idea: a regular seller would be protected once the buyer pulled, so הקדש is protected too.

steps.triggerLanguage: משכו במאתים ולא הספיק לפדותו עד שעמד במנה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of Case 1: the price drops instead of rising, and a new reason is used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once he pulled at 200, he is bound to pay 200 even if the price drops, since הקדש should be no weaker than a regular seller.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, לא יהא כח הדיוט חמור מהקדש, is exactly what the גמרא will use to challenge Case 4.

steps.title: Case 3: Paid 200, price dropped to 100 before pulling
steps.stepSummary: Someone paid 200 to redeem a הקדש item, and before he pulled it, the price dropped to 100. He pays 200, because the payment itself acquired it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he redeemed it at 200 and did not manage to pull it until it dropped to a מנה, he gives 200. What is the reason? 'He shall give the money and it will be his.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the ברייתא turns to cases where he paid first. Since money acquires from הקדש, the deal was done at 200, and the later price drop does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק from Case 1 now works the other way. Paying the money closed the deal right away at 200, so he cannot ask for the item at the new lower price.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeemed it, meaning he paid הקדש the money

phrases.english: If he redeemed it at two hundred,
and he did not manage to pull it
until it stood at a hundred –
he gives two hundred.
What is the reason?
"He shall give the money and it will be his."

steps.triggerLanguage: פדאו במאתים ולא הספיק למושכו עד שעמד במנה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from 'pulled first' cases to 'paid first' cases, again using the פסוק from Case 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Paying money acquires from הקדש immediately, so a later price drop does not change the price.

steps.title: Case 4: Paid 100, price rose to 200 before pulling
steps.stepSummary: Someone paid 100 to redeem a הקדש item, and before he pulled it, the price rose to 200. The redemption stands, and he pays only 100.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he redeemed it at a מנה and did not manage to pull it until it went up to 200, what he redeemed is redeemed, and he gives only a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last case and the one that helps the buyer. His money already acquired the item at 100, so the price rise does not affect him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because money acquires from הקדש, the deal closed at 100. Unlike the other three cases, here the outcome is good for the buyer, not for הקדש. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.whatToRemember: Four cases: (1) pulled at 100, rose to 200: pays 200. (2) Pulled at 200, dropped to 100: pays 200. (3) Paid 200, dropped to 100: pays 200. (4) Paid 100, rose to 200: pays only 100.

phrases.english: If he redeemed it at a hundred
and he did not manage to pull it
until it stood at two hundred –
what he redeemed is redeemed,
and he gives only a hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: פדאו במנה ולא הספיק למושכו עד שעמד במאתים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of Case 3: after paying, the price rises instead of dropping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money acquired the item at 100, so he pays only 100 even though the price rose before he pulled it.

steps.title: Why not apply the 'regular person is not stronger than הקדש' rule in Case 4?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why Case 4 lets the buyer pay only 100. It should say what Case 2 said: a regular person's power should not be stronger than הקדש's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let us say here too: the power of an ordinary person should not be stronger than הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Case 4 using the reason from Case 2. With a regular seller, money alone would not have closed the deal, so the seller could still demand the new price of 200. Why should הקדש get less?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Case 2, הקדש was given the protection that pulling gives a regular seller. Here too, a regular seller would be protected, because without pulling the sale is not final and he could ask for the higher price. So the same reasoning seems to require paying 200, which contradicts the ruling of Case 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? Used to open a challenge
Let us say the same here too

phrases.english: Why?
Let us say here too:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהֵא כֹּחַ הֶדְיוֹט חָמוּר מֵהֶקְדֵּשׁ?
phrases.english: The power of an ordinary person should not be stronger than הקדש!
phrases.notes: This is the same reason used in Case 2, now turned against Case 4.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמאי הכי נמי נימא לא יהא כח הדיוט חמור מהקדש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Case 4 using the reasoning from Case 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in Case 4 that he pays only a מנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Between regular people, money without pulling does not finalize a sale, so a seller could demand the risen price. The principle from Case 2 says הקדש should be no weaker than a regular seller, so he should pay 200.

steps.title: A regular seller who backs out is also under the curse of מי שפרע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a regular seller does not really have more power than הקדש. A seller who took the money and then backs out to ask for a higher price faces the curse of מי שפרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say a regular person is not under the curse of 'He Who exacted payment'? A regular seller who took the money and backs out is cursed too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6. A regular seller who has taken the money cannot simply back out to ask for 200, because whoever backs out after money was paid gets cursed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 argued that a regular seller could back out after receiving 100, since money alone does not finalize the sale, and so demand 200. The answer is that legally he could, but חז"ל curse whoever backs out after money was paid with מי שפרע. So the regular seller is not really stronger than הקדש, and הקדש need not get 200 here.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a rhetorical challenge)
'He Who exacted payment': a curse on someone who backs out of a deal after money was paid

steps.whatToRemember: A regular seller who took money and backs out is subject to the curse of מי שפרע, so he is not stronger than הקדש. That is why in Case 4 the buyer pays only 100. This closes the הקדש redemption discussion.

phrases.english: Is that to say that a regular person is not
standing under the curse of 'He Who exacted payment'?
phrases.notes: This is the curse on someone who backs out of a deal after money was paid. Here that is the seller, who would want more money once the price went up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ הֶדְיוֹט לָאו בְּמִי שֶׁפָּרַע קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the premise is wrong: the regular seller does not really have the power to back out, because of the curse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a regular seller who received money can legally back out and demand the higher price, a regular person looks stronger than הקדש, so the rule should have been applied in Case 4
steps.terutzMaskana: A regular seller who backs out after receiving money is under the curse of מי שפרע, so he is not really stronger than הקדש, and the rule does not require paying 200 in Case 4

steps.title: משנה: father-son מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says men are obligated and women are exempt in 'מצוות הבן על האב,' while both men and women are obligated in 'מצוות האב על הבן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All מצוות of the son upon the father: men are obligated and women are exempt. All מצוות of the father upon the son: both men and women are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its first rule is about father-son מצוות and who is obligated in them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two categories with opposite results for women. It does not explain what each phrase means, and the גמרא will soon ask exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: מצוות 'of the son upon the father'; the meaning is clarified in the גמרא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume yet that 'מצוות הבן על האב' means a son honoring his father. The גמרא is about to show that this reading causes a problem.

phrases.english: משנה:
All the מצוות of the son upon the father,
men are obligated and women are exempt.
And all the מצוות of the father upon the son:
both men and women are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מִצְוֹת הַבֵּן עַל הָאָב אֲנָשִׁים חַיָּיבִין וְנָשִׁים פְּטוּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Father-son מצוות of one type obligate only men, and of the other type obligate both men and women

steps.title: משנה: time-bound and non-time-bound positive מצוות
steps.stepSummary: Women are exempt from positive מצוות that depend on a set time, and obligated in positive מצוות that do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every positive מצוה caused by time: men are obligated and women are exempt. Every positive מצוה not caused by time: both men and women are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second general rule for positive מצוות, based on whether the מצוה is tied to a specific time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether time 'causes' the מצוה, meaning it can only be done at certain times. If it is tied to time, women are exempt. If not, women are obligated just like men.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment, something you must do
That time causes it; a מצוה done only at specific times

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the rule that women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות.

phrases.english: And every positive מצוה that time causes,
phrases.notes: He means a מצוה that applies only at certain times.

phrases.english: men are obligated and women are exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ –
phrases.english: And every positive מצוה that time does not cause:
both men and women are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a second rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות and obligated in positive מצוות that are not time-bound

steps.title: משנה: prohibitions apply to all, with three exceptions
steps.stepSummary: Men and women are equally bound by every לא תעשה, whether time-bound or not, except for rounding the head, destroying the beard, and becoming טמא to the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: All prohibitions, whether time-bound or not: both men and women are obligated, except 'do not round,' 'do not destroy,' and 'do not become טמא to the dead.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with prohibitions. Women are fully obligated in them, except for three listed prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The time-bound test from the previous rule does not apply to prohibitions at all. Only three specific prohibitions are limited to men: two about the head and beard, and the כהן's prohibition against becoming טמא to a dead body.

keyTerms.meaning: Prohibitions, things you must not do
Do not round off the corners of the head
Do not destroy the corners of the beard
Do not become טמא to the dead (said to כהנים)

steps.whatToRemember: Prohibitions bind women just like men, whether time-bound or not. The only exceptions are בל תקיף, בל תשחית, and בל תטמא למתים.

phrases.english: And all prohibitions,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ –
phrases.english: whether time causes them or time does not cause them:
both men and women are obligated,
except for 'do not round' and 'do not destroy,'
and 'do not become impure to the dead.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה בֵּין שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with the rule for prohibitions and its exceptions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All prohibitions apply to women too, except בל תקיף, בל תשחית, and בל תטמא למתים

steps.title: What does 'מצוות הבן על האב' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'מצוות הבן על האב' and suggests that it means duties a son must do for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'all מצוות of the son upon the father'? If you say it means all the מצוות a son must do for his father,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking what the משנה's first phrase means. It offers a first guess, which sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase could be read two ways. The first suggestion is that it means a child's duties toward a parent, such as honor and fear. The word אילימא ('if you say') signals that this suggestion is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be challenged)

phrases.english: גמרא:
What is 'all the מצוות of the son upon the father'?
If we say it means all the מצוות
that a son is obligated to do for his father,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כׇּל מִצְוֹת הַבֵּן עַל הָאָב אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's first phrase
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'מצוות הבן על האב': duties of a son toward his father, or something else

steps.title: A ברייתא shows women must fear their parents too
steps.stepSummary: If the phrase means a son's duties to his father, the משנה says women are exempt. But a ברייתא learns from the plural 'תיראו' that women must fear their parents too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are women exempt? But a ברייתא teaches: 'A man.' I only know a man; how do I know a woman? When it says 'A man, his mother and father you shall fear,' there are two here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first suggestion. A ברייתא proves that women are obligated in fearing parents, so they cannot be exempt from a son's duties to his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק starts with the singular 'איש' but uses the plural verb 'תיראו.' The ברייתא reads the plural as including two people: a man and a woman. That contradicts reading the משנה as exempting women from duties toward parents.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not from the word 'איש' but from the plural verb 'תיראו,' which shows more than one kind of person is being commanded.

phrases.english: are women exempt?
But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'A man':
I have only a man;
from where do I know a woman?
When it says:
'A man, his mother and his father you shall fear,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:3. 'You shall fear' is plural, even though 'a man' is singular.

phrases.english: here there are two!

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשִׁים פְּטוּרוֹת וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion made in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'מצוות הבן על האב' as a son's duties toward his father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the משנה exempt women from fearing and honoring parents, but the ברייתא derives from the plural 'תיראו' that women are obligated

steps.title: רב יהודה: the phrase means duties a father owes his son
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rereads the משנה: 'מצוות הבן על האב' means the duties about a son that are placed on the father. Men must do them, women are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what the משנה means. All the מצוות concerning a son that are placed on the father to do for his son: men are obligated and women are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 12 by giving the משנה's phrase a new meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 read the phrase as a son's duties to his father, but women must also honor and fear parents, so 'women are exempt' did not fit. רב יהודה flips the direction: the phrase means what a father must do for his son. A mother is not commanded in those duties, so 'women are exempt' now makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Used to explain the true meaning of a text
That are placed on the father

steps.confusionAlert: The same words 'מצוות הבן על האב' were first read as the son's duties to his father. Now they mean the father's duties about his son. The direction has flipped.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
This is what it is saying:
All the מצוות of the son
that are placed upon the father
to do for his son:
men are obligated and women are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה הכי קאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by reinterpreting the משנה's phrase.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase meant a son's duties toward his father, which women share.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase means a father's duties toward his son, which only the father (not the mother) carries.

steps.title: The ברייתא listing a father's duties to his son
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה, as רב יהודה reads it, teaches the ברייתא that lists a father's duties: מילה, פדיון הבן, teaching Torah, marrying him off, teaching a trade, and some add teaching him to swim.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have learned in our משנה what the רבנן taught: A father must, for his son, circumcise him, redeem him, teach him Torah, marry him to a woman, and teach him a trade. Some say: also teach him to swim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא listing a father's duties is exactly what our משנה means by 'מצוות הבן על האב.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fills in what the משנה's general phrase includes. It also backs up רב יהודה's reading, since a standard list of 'father's duties to his son' exists. The 'some say' opinion adds swimming as another basic way of protecting the son.

keyTerms.meaning: To redeem him (פדיון הבן for a firstborn)
To marry him off to a wife
Some say. Introduces an extra opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the basic map of a father's obligations, and the גמרא will now go through these duties one by one to find their sources.

phrases.english: We have learned that which the Rabbis taught:
A father is obligated regarding his son
to circumcise him, and to redeem him,
and to teach him Torah,
and to marry him to a woman,
and to teach him a trade.
And some say:
also to teach him to swim in water.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנינא להא דתנו רבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב יהודה's reading of the משנה matches a known ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father must circumcise, redeem, teach Torah, marry off, and teach a trade to his son; some add swimming.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: no trade means teaching him to steal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that a father who does not teach his son a trade teaches him banditry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Anyone who does not teach his son a trade teaches him banditry.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, רבי יהודה adds a strong statement about how important it is to teach a trade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links not teaching a trade with robbery. Taken literally, this sounds extreme, and the גמרא will question it in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְלַמֵּד אֶת בְּנוֹ אוּמָּנוּת –
phrases.english: Anyone who does not teach his son a trade
teaches him banditry.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהודה אומר כל שאינו מלמד את בנו אומנות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with an added opinion on teaching a trade.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Failing to teach a son a trade is linked to teaching him robbery.

steps.title: Does he really teach him to steal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: can it really mean the father actually teaches his son banditry?
steps.simpleTranslation: Banditry? Can that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the literal wording of רבי יהודה's statement, setting up a clarification in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father who simply does not teach a trade is not actively training his son to rob. So the literal words cannot be right, and the גמרא wants a better reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Can it enter your mind? A way of saying 'that can't be right'

phrases.english: Banditry, can it enter your mind?

steps.triggerLanguage: ליסטות סלקא דעתך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the literal meaning of רבי יהודה's words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal wording 'teaches him banditry' in רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not teaching a trade is passive; it cannot literally be teaching him to rob.

steps.title: It is as if he teaches him to steal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: it is as though he teaches him banditry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is as if he teaches him banditry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: רבי יהודה was speaking in a 'it's as if' way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father is not literally teaching robbery. But a son with no way to earn a living may end up stealing, so the result is as bad as if the father had taught him to steal.
steps.whatToRemember: A father must teach his son a trade; leaving him without one is treated as if he taught him to steal.

phrases.english: Rather: it is as if he teaches him banditry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא כאילו מלמדו ליסטות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the words as a comparison, not literally
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father literally teaches his son robbery.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is only 'as if' he teaches robbery, because the son may turn to stealing.

steps.title: Where do we learn the father must circumcise his son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins going through the list, asking for the source that a father must perform מילה on his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To circumcise him': from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts looking for a פסוק behind each item on the list, beginning with מילה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated the duties without sources. Now the גמרא wants to see where in the Torah the father's duty of מילה comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: 'To circumcise him': from where do we derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: למולו מנלן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list to finding a source for its first item.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that a father must circumcise his son.

steps.title: אברהם circumcised his son יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק that אברהם circumcised his son יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And אברהם circumcised his son יצחק.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק showing a father circumcising his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses that the father, אברהם, did the מילה on 'his son.' That shows the duty lies first on the father.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דכתיב ויימל אברהם את יצחק בנו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ויימל אברהם את יצחק בנו' shows the father must circumcise his son.

steps.title: If the father doesn't, the court must
steps.stepSummary: If the father did not circumcise his son, the בית דין must do it, learned from 'every male among you shall be circumcised.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Where his father did not circumcise him, the בית דין must circumcise him, as it is written: 'Every male among you shall be circumcised.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second level: the duty passes to the בית דין when the father fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'among you' (לכם) speaks to the whole people, not just the father. So the community, through the בית דין, carries the duty as a backup.

phrases.english: And where his father did not circumcise him
the court is obligated to circumcise him,
as it is written: 'Every male among you shall be circumcised.'

steps.triggerLanguage: והיכא דלא מהליה אבוה מיחייבי בי דינא למימהליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the father's duty of מילה to the בית דין as a backup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the father does not circumcise his son, the בית דין must.

steps.title: If the court doesn't, he must circumcise himself
steps.stepSummary: If the בית דין also did not circumcise him, the son himself must do it, learned from the פסוק that an uncircumcised male gets כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where the בית דין did not circumcise him, he himself must circumcise himself, as it is written: 'And an uncircumcised male who does not circumcise the flesh of his foreskin, shall be cut off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third level: in the end, the duty falls on the son himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק punishes the uncircumcised man himself with כרת. That only makes sense if he personally has a duty to become circumcised once no one else did it.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall be cut off (כרת)

steps.whatToRemember: מילה has three levels of responsibility: first the father, then the בית דין, and finally the son himself.

phrases.english: And where the court did not circumcise him
he himself is obligated to circumcise himself,
as it is written: 'And the uncircumcised male who will not circumcise
the flesh of his foreskin, shall be cut off.'

steps.triggerLanguage: והיכא דלא מהלוה בי דינא מיחייב איהו למימהל נפשיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final level after the father and the בית דין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the בית דין does not circumcise him, the son must circumcise himself.

steps.title: Where do we learn the mother is not obligated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a mother is not obligated to circumcise her son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her, from where do we know she is not obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects back to the משנה's rule that women are exempt from a father's duties, and asks for a source in the case of מילה. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said women are exempt from these duties. Now the גמרא wants a specific source for that in the case of מילה.

phrases.english: She, from where do we derive that she is not obligated?

steps.triggerLanguage: איהי מנלן דלא מיחייבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who must do מילה to who is exempt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a mother is not obligated to circumcise her son.

steps.title: 'As God commanded him', not her
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'as God commanded him,' meaning him and not her, so the mother is not obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'As God commanded him.' Him, and not her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק's word 'him' limits the command to the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק about אברהם ends 'as God commanded him.' The word 'him' is read as excluding the mother, which fits רב יהודה's rule that women are exempt from a father's duties toward his son.
steps.whatToRemember: The mother is not obligated in her son's מילה, because the פסוק says God commanded 'him' (the father).

phrases.english: As it is written: 'As God commanded him':
phrases.notes: בראשית 21:4, the same פסוק about אברהם and יצחק.

phrases.english: him, and not her.

steps.triggerLanguage: דכתיב כאשר צוה אותו אלהים אותו ולא אותה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אותו' in the פסוק excludes the mother: him and not her.

steps.title: Where do we learn that מילה applies for all generations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: we found the command of מילה given at that moment to אברהם, but where do we see it applies to later generations too?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for right then. Where do we learn it for future generations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the last source, 'as God commanded him,' was said about אברהם himself. It asks how we know the מצוה continues for all later generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in step 23 describes what אברהם did in his own time. A story about one person does not automatically make a law for everyone forever, so the גמרא needs a source for future generations.

phrases.english: We found [a source for] right then;
phrases.notes: He means the time of אברהם, from the פסוק 'as God commanded him' in the last step.

phrases.english: for [later] generations, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן מִיָּד, לְדוֹרוֹת מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the source from step 23 and asks how far it reaches in time.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the command of מילה given to אברהם is binding on all future generations.

steps.title: The word 'command' means urging, for now and for all generations
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that wherever the תורה says צו, it means strong urging that applies right away and for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: wherever it says 'command,' it means urging, both right away and for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a general rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל about the word צו. Since the מילה פסוק uses that word ('as God commanded him'), it applies forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule gives the word צו two meanings at once: extra urging, and a law that lasts for all generations. Because צו appears in the פסוק about אברהם's מילה, that מצוה is not limited to his time.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
Urging, pushing someone to act with energy

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule about צו is a general tool. The גמרא can use it any time the תורה uses that word, not only for מילה.

phrases.english: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Any place where it says 'command,'
it means nothing other than urging,
right away and for all generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״צַו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word צו in the מילה פסוק means urging that applies right away and for all generations.

steps.title: Proofs that 'command' means urging and lasts for generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings one פסוק showing that צו means urging, and another showing that it means right away and for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Urging, as it says: 'Command יהושע, and encourage him and strengthen him.' Right away and for generations, as it says: 'From the day that God commanded and onward, for your generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up each half of the rule of רבי ישמעאל's school with its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יהושע פסוק, 'command' sits next to 'encourage' and 'strengthen,' so it means urging. In the second פסוק, 'commanded' is tied to 'from the day onward, for your generations,' so it means a law that starts now and lasts forever.

keyTerms.meaning: And encourage him and strengthen him

steps.whatToRemember: The command of מילה applies to every generation, because the פסוק uses the word צו, which means urging both right away and forever.

phrases.english: [That it means] urging, as it is written:
'And command יהושע, and encourage him and strengthen him.'
[That it means] right away and for generations, as it is written:
'From the day that God commanded'
'and onward, for your generations.'

steps.triggerLanguage: זֵירוּז, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְצַו אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְחַזְּקֵהוּ וְאַמְּצֵהוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק for each part of the rule in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that צו means urging, right away and for generations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 3:28 for urging; במדבר 15:23 for right away and for generations.

steps.title: Where do we learn the father must redeem his son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next obligation in the ברייתא, that a father must redeem his firstborn son, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: To redeem him. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts a new topic. It quotes the next duty listed in the ברייתא, פדיון הבן, and asks for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed several things a father must do for his son. Having finished מילה, the גמרא goes on to the next item, redeeming a firstborn son, and asks which פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: To redeem him (פדיון הבן of a firstborn son)
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: [The ברייתא said the father must] redeem him. From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: לִפְדּוֹתוֹ. מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of מילה and opens the next item from the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a father must redeem his firstborn son.

steps.title: The פסוק: 'Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem'
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק commanding that every firstborn of 'your sons' be redeemed, which speaks to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that tells a person to redeem the firstborn of his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'your sons' show that the פסוק is talking to the father. So the father is the one obligated to redeem his firstborn.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״כׇּל בְּכוֹר בָּנֶיךָ תִּפְדֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem' obligates the father.

steps.title: If the father did not redeem him, the son must redeem himself
steps.stepSummary: If the father did not redeem his firstborn, the son himself is obligated to do it, learned from the wording of a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where his father did not redeem him, he must redeem himself, as it is written: 'you shall be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new rule: when the father failed to redeem the son, the duty passes to the son himself. This is just like the rule for מילה in step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's wording is read as speaking to the firstborn himself: 'you shall be redeemed.' That shows the redemption must happen no matter what, so if the father did not do it, the son has to.

phrases.english: And where his father did not redeem him,
he is obligated to redeem himself,
as it is written: 'you shall be redeemed.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:15. The printed גמרא has the word פָּדֹה in round brackets. The corrected wording leaves it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא דְּלָא פַּרְקֵיהּ אֲבוּהּ מִיחַיַּיב אִיהוּ לְמִפְרְקֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the father's duty from step 28 to the son when the father failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the father did not redeem his firstborn, the son must redeem himself.

steps.title: Where do we learn the mother is not obligated to redeem?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a mother is not commanded to redeem her firstborn son.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for her, from where do we know that she is not commanded?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as it did for מילה in step 22, the גמרא asks how we know that the mother has no duty to redeem her son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'every firstborn of your sons' could in theory speak to either parent. So the גמרא needs a source that leaves the mother out.

phrases.english: And for her, from where do we know that she is not commanded?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיהִי מְנָלַן דְּלָא מִיפַּקְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same question about the mother that step 22 asked about מילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a mother is not obligated to redeem her firstborn son.

steps.title: Only someone who must redeem himself must redeem others
steps.stepSummary: The word תפדה can also be read תיפדה, 'you shall be redeemed.' This teaches that only someone who is commanded to redeem himself is commanded to redeem others, which leaves out the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written 'you shall be redeemed' / 'you shall redeem': whoever is commanded to redeem himself is commanded to redeem others, and whoever is not commanded to redeem himself is not commanded to redeem others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads one word in two ways and ties them together. The person who must redeem others is the same kind of person who could need to redeem himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same letters spell 'you shall redeem' and 'you shall be redeemed,' so the two duties go together. A woman is never commanded to redeem herself as a firstborn, so she is not commanded to redeem her son either.
steps.whatToRemember: פדיון הבן follows the same pattern as מילה: the father must do it, the son must do it himself if the father did not, and the mother is not obligated.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a mistake in spelling. The גמרא is deliberately reading the same letters both ways, 'redeem' and 'be redeemed,' to link the two duties.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'you shall be redeemed' / 'you shall redeem.'
phrases.notes: The same letters can be read both ways, and the גמרא uses both readings.

phrases.english: Whoever is commanded to redeem himself
is commanded to redeem others,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְצֻוֶּוה לִפְדּוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ –
phrases.english: and whoever is not commanded to redeem himself
is not commanded to redeem others.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״תִּיפָּדֶה״ – ״תִּפְדֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reading תפדה also as תיפדה links redeeming oneself to redeeming others. A woman is not commanded to redeem herself, so she is not commanded to redeem her son.

steps.title: Why is a woman not obligated to redeem herself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a woman has no duty to redeem herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for her, how do we know that she is not obligated to redeem herself?
steps.whatsHappening: An unredeemed son must redeem himself (Step 29), so the גמרא asks why a woman has no such duty. This question sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 asked about a mother redeeming her son. Now the question turns to the woman herself. It asks where we learn that she has no obligation to redeem her own self.

phrases.english: And she, from where do we know
phrases.notes: 'She' is a woman. Compare the son in Step 29, who must redeem himself if his father didn't.

phrases.english: that she is not obligated to redeem herself?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיהִי מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the mother's duty toward her son to the woman's duty toward herself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a woman is not obligated to redeem herself.

steps.title: The reading תיפדה links redeeming others to redeeming oneself
steps.stepSummary: Reading תפדה as תיפדה teaches that only someone whom others must redeem must redeem himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'You shall redeem,' which can be read 'You shall be redeemed.' Anyone whom others are commanded to redeem is commanded to redeem himself. Anyone whom others are not commanded to redeem is not commanded to redeem himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same double reading of the פסוק from Step 31, but now in the other direction. It ties a person's duty to redeem himself to whether others must redeem him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 31 the reading showed that only someone obligated to redeem himself must redeem others. Here it shows that only someone whom others must redeem has to redeem himself. To finish the answer, we still need to prove that nobody has to redeem a woman.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same תפדה / תיפדה reading as Step 31, but it is used here for a new point. Step 31 went from 'redeem yourself' to 'redeem others.' This step goes from 'others redeem you' to 'redeem yourself.'

phrases.english: As it is written: 'You shall redeem,' read as 'You shall be redeemed,'
anyone whom others are commanded to redeem
is commanded to redeem himself,
and anyone whom others are not commanded to redeem
is not commanded to redeem himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב תִּפְדֶּה תִּיפָּדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 32 by setting out a general rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person must redeem himself only if others are commanded to redeem him.

steps.title: How do we know others need not redeem a woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that nobody is commanded to redeem a daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that others are not commanded to redeem her?
steps.whatsHappening: The rule from Step 33 only works if nobody has to redeem a woman. So the גמרא asks for the source for that missing piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 depends on a fact it did not prove. This question asks for that fact.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that others are not commanded to redeem her?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין אֲחֵרִים מְצֻוִּוין לִפְדּוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the missing piece that the rule in Step 33 relies on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that no one is commanded to redeem a daughter.

steps.title: Your sons, and not your daughters
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'firstborn of your sons,' which leaves out daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem.' This means your sons, and not your daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the word בניך, 'your sons,' to show that the מצוה applies only to sons. Since nobody has to redeem a daughter, she does not have to redeem herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the argument. Nobody must redeem a daughter, and by the rule in Step 33, she therefore has no duty to redeem herself.
steps.whatToRemember: A woman has no פדיון הבן obligation, not for her son and not for herself. Only someone whom others must redeem has to redeem himself, and the פסוק limits redemption to sons.

phrases.english: As the verse states: 'Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem'
your sons, and not your daughters.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא כׇּל בְּכוֹר בָּנֶיךָ תִּפְדֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 34 and finishes the proof that began in Step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Your sons' leaves out daughters, so nobody has to redeem them, and so they need not redeem themselves.

steps.title: A father redeems himself before his son
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if a man must redeem both himself and his son, he comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he needs to be redeemed and his son needs to be redeemed, he comes before his son.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא opens a new topic: which redemption comes first. This first opinion says the father redeems himself first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a firstborn who was never redeemed and now has his own firstborn son. If he has money for only one redemption, the תנא קמא says he redeems himself first.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If he is to be redeemed and his son is to be redeemed,
he takes precedence over his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הוּא לִפְדּוֹת וּבְנוֹ לִפְדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 29, which says a son must redeem himself, and asks what happens when that clashes with redeeming his own son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a man must redeem both himself and his son, he redeems himself first.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the son comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says the son comes first, because that מצוה is directly on the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: His son comes before him. The מצוה of redeeming the father was really on the father's own father, but the מצוה of redeeming his son is on him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the opposite ruling and explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's own redemption was first his father's job, and it only fell to him because his father never did it. Redeeming his son is his own direct מצוה from the start, so רבי יהודה says that one comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה of redeeming him was on his father
the מצוה of his son is on him

steps.whyThisMatters: The two opinions disagree about how to rank מצוות. Is the stronger one my own personal redemption, or the מצוה that was placed on me directly from the start?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: His son takes precedence over him.
For this one, his מצוה is upon his father,
and that one, the מצוה of his son is upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בְּנוֹ קוֹדְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the תנא קמא of Step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The son is redeemed first, because that מצוה falls directly on the father, while the father's own redemption was originally his father's duty.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה begins: everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה starts to say what everyone agrees on in this מחלוקת. His statement continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Everyone agrees...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only the opening. רבי ירמיה is about to name a case where the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה do not disagree, and the rest comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Everyone agrees' tells us the coming statement will limit the מחלוקת to a certain case. The details are not given yet.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya says:
Everyone agrees

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הַכֹּל מוֹדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to narrow the מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not finished yet. It introduces a case where both sides agree.
